headline: ByteDance training massive AI model to rival Anthropic's Mythos
summary: The TikTok parent is reportedly training an AI model with up to 10 trillion parameters, aiming to compete with leading US AI labs.
details: ByteDance is reportedly in the early stages of training a massive AI model with up to 10 trillion parameters. This scale is three times larger than China's current biggest model, Moonshot's Kimi K3, and aims to rival Anthropic's advanced systems like Mythos 5.

While parameter count is a key indicator of an AI model's capacity, actual performance also hinges on data quality and training methodologies. ByteDance's approach focuses on independent development rather than distilling existing models, a strategy they believe will lead to superior capabilities.

The company has been investing heavily in AI over the past three years, expanding its data centers and hiring top researchers. Its SeeDance model is already advanced in video generation, and its consumer-facing Doubao model boasts over 300 million monthly active users in China.

ByteDance's management, including founder Zhang Yiming, is committed to long-term development of world-leading AI capabilities. This ambitious project underscores the growing competition and rapid advancement of AI research in China, with local labs striving to not only catch up but also outperform their US counterparts.

headline_marked: US Economy [[Lost 23,000 Jobs]] in July, Reversing Gains
headline: US Economy Lost 23,000 Jobs in July, Reversing Gains
summary: Economists expected 83,000 new jobs, but the labor market saw a sudden reversal. Previous months' figures were also revised down significantly.
details: The U.S. economy shed 23,000 jobs in July, a stark reversal after four months of positive growth. This figure fell significantly short of the 83,000 jobs economists had predicted.

Adding to the concern, the Bureau of Labor Statistics revised down the job gains for May and June by a combined 103,000 roles. May's total was cut by 66,000 to 129,000, and June's by 37,000 to 57,000.
Wage growth also showed signs of stalling, with average hourly earnings rising only 0.1% from June and 3.2% year-over-year. This pace is below the current inflation rate of 3.5%.

The labor force participation rate dropped to its lowest point since February 2021, indicating that workers are increasingly leaving the workforce. This trend, coupled with elevated energy prices due to ongoing geopolitical tensions, paints a challenging economic picture.

Significant job losses were seen in local government education (-50,000), retail (-19,000), and the financial industry (-14,000). The leisure and hospitality sector also contracted by 40,000 jobs, a potential warning sign for consumer spending.

While health care employment continued to rise, it did so at a slower pace. Modest gains were noted in manufacturing (+5,000) and construction (+22,000), with some industries benefiting from the AI data center boom.

The disappointing jobs report led to a sharp rise in stock futures and a drop in bond yields, as investors anticipated the Federal Reserve might hold off on raising interest rates. Odds of a September rate hike fell from over 50% to around 40%.
